findings.text: the a-crew row states a denominator of 10 but names only nine counted sections (s2, s3, s4, s5, s6, s7, s9, s10, s11) and the record's own embedded command, re-run at the stated head, prints 9 for that plan — s1 is excluded as done and s8 as deferred under the rule the method states — so one of seventeen rows is still not reproducible by the instrument this round added, and the misstatement also inverts two keep reasons: :124 "six of ten sections unlanded, the largest remaining count in the batch" and :288 "second only to the crew-process plan" both read the other way at the correct 4 of 9, which leaves five unlanded against the six the review-dies row carries.

the a-dispatch row counts 6 of 9 present while four of those six carry no file and symbol — s2 and s3 are asserted from the plan's own "declared done" status, which the method at :68-69 says the reading does not use, and s9 and s10 cite a bare file with no symbol — so the done-when's "cites the file and symbol that shows each counted one present" holds for two counted sections of six; the same shape remains at :150 (a-dry-run, whose counted s2 is cited as a file only while the row's own text says it "stops before the resolutions s2 names"), :171 (a-follower-outlives, "s5 done, no change needed" with no citation and s6 cited by the absence of a marker at :172), and :280 (a-review-dies, s2 with no citation at all).

the a-review-dies row cites reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5799 for EXIT_RECORD_NAME but that name is defined at dispatch.py:5859 at the stated head, 5799 falling inside _start_backend's docstring, so the line a reader opens is not the symbol the citation names.

the plan's section 2 landing beat still reads "keep 13, merge 2 ... close 2" and "the batch keep count is 13" while the record landed this round reads keep 6 / merge 9 / close 2; the node was fenced out of editing any plan and declares the staleness under follow_ons, so nothing is hidden, but until the owning session corrects the beat the plan and its own evidence record disagree on the number the lead sums across the four batches.
